### fable-2-1
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/TerminalEnv.ts:30
- class: jsdoc   severity: required
- standard: .patterns/jsdoc-documentation.md (Examples teach the API; Example code is Effect-pattern code the docgen gate compiles); section 10.2 (every value-level export has an observable, compiling Example)   evidence: Lines 30-32 sit inside the `/** ... */` block of `StreamEnv` without the ` * ` prefix: `import * as P from "effect/Predicate";`, `import * as SchemaGetter from "effect/SchemaGetter";`, `import { identity } from "effect/Function";`. `git show ce9331673c -- scratchpad/effected/env/TerminalEnv.ts` shows the S3 import insertion was applied after every occurrence of `import * as S from "effect/Schema";`, including the one inside the Example fence. A read-only TypeScript parse (`ts.getJSDocCommentsAndTags` on the StreamEnv statement) returns the comment with those three lines inside the ```ts fence, so docgen renders an Example whose first five lines are imports of which three (`P`, `SchemaGetter`, `identity`) are unused. The docgen gate compiles the example and unused imports are not compile errors, so the gate cannot see it.
- failure: The published StreamEnv Example shows three unused imports (`P`, `SchemaGetter`, `identity`) and un-prefixed lines in the source comment; the docs teach the wrong usage and the comment block is visibly corrupted in hovers.
- fix: Delete lines 30-32 of TerminalEnv.ts (the three un-prefixed import lines inside the JSDoc). The real imports at lines 9-11 stay only while fable-2-2 is open; after fable-2-2 they go too.

### fable-2-2
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/TerminalEnv.ts:68
- class: schema   severity: required
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 17 (prefer built-in schema constructors/checks) and law 21 (tersest equivalent form); SCHEMA.md:2321 (`Schema.declare` is for a type that does not fit the built-in combinators); node_modules/effect/dist/Schema.d.ts:2612 (`S.Number` is the schema for number values including NaN, Infinity, -Infinity); D9   evidence: `columns: S.Option(S.declare(P.isNumber, { ...$I.annote("StreamColumns", ...), toCodecArbitrary: () => S.link<number>()(S.Finite, { decode: SchemaGetter.transform(identity), encode: SchemaGetter.transform(identity) }) }))` hand-declares the primitive `number`, which `S.Number` already is with the identical domain (its JSDoc: including NaN and both infinities). `git show ce9331673c` shows S1/S2 shipped the bare `S.declare(P.isNumber, ...)` and S3 bolted on `toCodecArbitrary` plus three imports because a bare declaration cannot derive an arbitrary (read-only probe: `Arbitrary.schema(S.Struct({ columns: S.Option(S.declare((u) => typeof u === "number")) }))` fails with `Unable to derive an arbitrary for an unsupported Declaration`). Read-only probe from scratchpad/ with `bun -e` against the installed effect: `S.Option(S.Number)` in the same struct round-trips 500 `Arbitrary.sampleEffect` samples (1 NaN among them) under `S.toEquivalence` + `deepStrictEqual` exactly as the lab schema does; `S.toEquivalence(S.Number)(NaN, NaN) === true`; `S.fromJsonString` of both structs encodes identically; `S.is` accepts NaN columns for both. Upstream StreamEnv.columns is `Option<number>`.
- failure: A bespoke declaration (`StreamColumns` identity, custom guard, custom arbitrary link, three extra imports and the `effect/SchemaGetter` dependency) stands in for `S.Number`; the derived JSON Schema/representation of StreamEnv is an opaque declaration instead of the standard number keyword, and every reader has to work out that the custom type is just `number`.
- fix: Replace lines 68-73 with `columns: S.Option(S.Number).pipe($I.annoteKey("StreamEnv.columns", { description: "The terminal width in columns, or None when it is unknown." })),` and drop the `P`, `SchemaGetter` and `identity` imports (lines 9-11). TerminalEnv.property.test.ts and TerminalEnv.coverage.test.ts keep passing unchanged (probe above); the identity-annotations deviation text that lists `StreamColumns` needs the one word removed.

### fable-2-3
- file: scratchpad/test/env/Audience.test.ts:16
- class: law   severity: required
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 6 (no native Set/Map); scratchpad/EFFECTED_PORT_GOAL.md section 16 ("never use native Set/Map") and the 2026-10-09 ruling that `Logger.CurrentLoggers` sites use `Logger.layer`; AGENTS.md Code Laws; D9 (upstream shape is the contract)   evidence: Audience.test.ts:13-21 `capture = (lines) => Layer.succeed(Logger.CurrentLoggers, new Set([Logger.make(...)]))` and EnvOverride.test.ts:13-18 `capture = (lines) => new Set([Logger.make(...)])` provided through `Effect.provideService(Logger.CurrentLoggers, capture(lines))`. The upstream oracle (`__test__/Audience.test.ts`, `__test__/EnvOverride.test.ts`) wrote `Logger.layer([Logger.make(...)])`; the S3 commit replaced the Effect API with a native `Set`. `Logger.layer` is stable installed API (node_modules/effect/dist/Logger.d.ts:828, returns `Layer<never, never, never>` for plain loggers) and other lab modules use it under the same canon (scratchpad/test/github-actions/PackageManagerInstaller.test.ts:790, CheckDocument.test.ts:484). The gate missed it because the native-runtime law skips test files: `bun run beep laws native-runtime --check --include "scratchpad/test/env/Audience.test.ts,scratchpad/test/env/EnvOverride.test.ts,scratchpad/test/env/agentCi.test.ts,scratchpad/effected/env/Audience.ts"` reports `scanned_files=1`, and `TYPESCRIPT_SOURCE_EXCLUDED_SUFFIXES` (repo-utils TypeScriptSourceExclusions.ts:67-70) excludes `.test.ts`.
- failure: The S3 canon migration introduced two new native `Set` constructions that upstream never had, replacing `Logger.layer` with a hand-built `CurrentLoggers` value; the law gate cannot report them because it does not scan tests, so the only barrier was review.
- fix: In both files: `const capture = (lines) => Logger.layer([Logger.make(...)])`. Audience.test.ts already composes it with `Layer.provide(capture(lines))`, which accepts the Layer as is. In EnvOverride.test.ts replace the two `Effect.provideService(...)` calls in `read`/`result` (lines 27-31, 89-93) and the four inline sites with one `Effect.provide(Layer.mergeAll(Audience.layerTest(kind), capture(lines)))` so no `multipleEffectProvide` diagnostic returns; import `effect/Layer`.

### fable-2-4
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/internal/osc8/detect.ts:57
- class: schema   severity: required
- standard: standards/effect-first-development.md EF-33 (schema first for property-based domain shapes; derive types instead of parallel interfaces); standards/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 / schema-first-development-prompt (Schema owns pure data); standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 19 (LiteralKit for named domains referenced by name); round-1 INVENTORY env-10/env-12 (same standard applied to this file's sibling payloads) and env-1 (AudienceShape.source, a field domain referenced as `Shape["field"]`)   evidence: `export interface Osc8Info` (detect.ts:57-130) is the exported result record of `detect`: eleven pure-data fields (booleans, `Osc8Reason`, strings, `KnownTerminal | null`, `WrapperInfo | null`, `Osc8Capabilities`, and the inline literal union `override: "force-hyperlink" | "no-hyperlink" | "no-color" | null` at :123). Every one of its sub-domains now has a schema (Osc8Reason, KnownTerminal, WrapperInfo, Osc8Capabilities), and its siblings ProcessSnapshot (:148) and Osc8Detection (:284) were converted to identity-annotated `S.Struct`s in the round-1 fix wave under exactly this standard, yet Osc8Info stayed an interface. The `override` domain is referenced by name at :182 (`readonly override: Osc8Info["override"]` in Gate), the shape round-1 env-1 ruled a named domain. osc8.detect.test.ts:19/35/46 pins the three override strings and `null`.
- failure: The module's richest pure payload has no schema source of truth, no `S.is`, no arbitrary (D10 floor cannot cover it), and its `override` literal domain is a hand-written union referenced by name, so the osc8 payloads are modeled under two different disciplines in one file.
- fix: Add `export const Osc8Override = LiteralKit(["force-hyperlink", "no-hyperlink", "no-color"]).annotate($I.annote("Osc8Override", {...}))` + `export type Osc8Override = typeof Osc8Override.Type`; define `export const Osc8Info = S.Struct({ supported: S.Boolean, supportedForStderr: S.Boolean, reason: Osc8Reason, explanation: S.String, terminal: S.NullOr(KnownTerminal), terminalRaw: S.NullOr(S.String), terminalVersion: S.NullOr(S.String), wrapper: S.NullOr(WrapperInfo), isStdoutTTY: S.Boolean, isStderrTTY: S.Boolean, override: S.NullOr(Osc8Override), capabilities: Osc8Capabilities })` with `$I.annoteKey` on each field and `.annotate($I.annote("Osc8Info", ...))`, `export type Osc8Info = typeof Osc8Info.Type`; change the type-only imports of KnownTerminal/WrapperInfo/Osc8Capabilities to value imports; `Gate.override` becomes `Osc8Override | null`. `detect` keeps returning the same plain object. Add the two round-trip properties (Osc8Override, Osc8Info) to scratchpad/test/env/internal/osc8/detect.property.test.ts per D10 and a titled Example per the JSDoc law.

### fable-2-5
- file: scratchpad/test/env/RuntimeEnv.test.ts:198
- class: test   severity: required
- standard: scratchpad/EFFECTED_PORT_GOAL.md operator ruling 2026-10-09 ("Deliberate wrong-input casts in tests go through one deliberatelyInvalid<T> helper per module ... and nothing else"); D15 (no hidden `any`); section 11.1/11.2 (tests keep upstream meaning)   evidence: Upstream `__test__/RuntimeEnv.test.ts:148-151` feeds the invalid CI through `// @ts-expect-error ...` + `RuntimeEnv.make({ ..., ci: Option.some("jenkins"), ... })`. The lab rewrote it as `Reflect.apply(RuntimeEnv.make, RuntimeEnv, [{ agent: O.none(), ci: O.some("jenkins"), terminal: O.none() }])`: `Reflect.apply`'s `argumentsList: ArrayLike<any>` erases the parameter type, so the deliberately invalid input passes the compiler through a lib.d.ts `any` that the D15 scanner cannot see. Five other lab modules carry the sanctioned helper (`scratchpad/test/{cli,config-file,engine,github,github-actions}/deliberatelyInvalid.ts`, the one `value as T` per module), and `@ts-expect-error` itself remains in use under the same gates (scratchpad/test/cli/Doc.test.ts:72, github-actions/GitHubMarkdown.test.ts:167), so nothing forced the detour; `.oxlintrc.json` enables no category that bans the directive.
- failure: The module's only deliberately ill-typed input is hidden behind a reflective call instead of the one named helper the ruling designates, so the site is unfindable by the agreed search (`deliberatelyInvalid`) and the type erasure is invisible to the D15 gate.
- fix: Add `scratchpad/test/env/deliberatelyInvalid.ts` (copy the cli module's helper verbatim) and write `const unknown = () => RuntimeEnv.make(deliberatelyInvalid<Parameters<typeof RuntimeEnv.make>[0]>({ agent: O.none(), ci: O.some("jenkins"), terminal: O.none() }));`.

### fable-2-6
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/internal/agentCi.ts:29
- class: effect-idiom   severity: backlog
- standard: standards/effect-laws-v1.md law 21 (tersest equivalent form); D11 (maintenance preference without behaviour change)   evidence: `CiNameBase = LiteralKit([...])` (:12) exists only so `CiName = CiNameBase.annotate({ ...$I.annote("CiName", ...), message: \`Expected ${A.join(A.map(CiNameBase.literals, (name) => \`"${name}"\`), " | ")}\` })` can spell a custom message. ### fable-2-7
- file: scratchpad/effected/env/internal/osc8/detect.ts:290
- class: schema   severity: backlog
- standard: Operator step 4 (identity annotations with stable identities); @beep/identity Id.ts (`annote` mints `identifier`/`schemaId` from the segment; IdentityRegistry fails on duplicate keys)   evidence: The nested terminal struct is annotated `$I.annote("Osc8Detection.terminal", ...)` and the enclosing `S.Option(...)` field is annotated `$I.annoteKey("Osc8Detection.terminal", ...)` on the same line, so one identifier (`.../internal/osc8/detect/Osc8Detection.terminal`) names two different things: the inner struct schema and the outer Option field. RuntimeEnv.ts keeps them apart (`DetectedTerminal` for the struct, `RuntimeEnv.terminal` for the key).
